title: Russian Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) Cyber Operations: Trends and Best Practices for Network Defenders
canonical_title: Russian Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) Cyber Operations: Trends and Best Practices for Network Defenders
raw_text: CISA and international intelligence partners have identified persistent malicious cyber activities conducted by Russian Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) actors, also known as APT29 or Cozy Bear. APT29 targets government, diplomatic, think-tank, and healthcare organizations globally. In their campaigns, APT29 deployed custom backdoor malware families known as WellMess and WellMail to exfiltrate intelligence and command compromised systems. The actors gained entry by exploiting external network vulnerabilities, notably CVE-2019-19781 in Citrix Application Delivery Controller and Gateway appliances, as well as CVE-2020-0688 in Microsoft Exchange Server. Following successful exploitation, APT29 uses PowerShell scripts to harvest local credentials and stage encrypted archives for remote exfiltration.
